name: louvain
author: e7c02e9e
description: Finds communities (densely connected groups of nodes) using the Louvain modularity-optimisation algorithm implemented from scratch. Use it to answer questions such as 'what communities exist in this network?', 'what natural groups are present?', 'which community does node X belong to?' or 'how strong is the community structure?'. Works on undirected graphs and also accepts directed graphs, treating their edges as undirected. Supports weighted graphs; set use_weights=false when weights represent distances or costs rather than connection strengths. Returns the number of communities, modularity, and the largest top_k communities with their sizes, representative members and registered subgraph IDs. If node is supplied, its community is also reported and listed even if it falls outside the top_k largest communities. result_graph_id identifies the largest community.

graph_id.description: ID of the graph to analyse.

resolution.description: Positive community-size control parameter. 1.0 is standard modularity; larger values generally favour more and smaller communities, while smaller values generally favour fewer and larger communities.

use_weights.description: If true, edge weights are used as connection strengths when the graph is weighted. Set false when weights represent distances or costs rather than connection strengths.

seed.description: Random seed controlling the node visitation order. The same graph, parameters and seed produce deterministic results.

top_k.description: Maximum number of largest communities to list in detail. If node is supplied and its community is outside the top_k, that community is also listed.

node.description: Optional node ID. If provided, the result also identifies its community and size. Use lookup_node to find the ID from a node name.
